title: The Sharp Extraction
premise: Lior Eriksen, a freelance interpreter who quietly handles the peace process's dirty work, receives a call on a burner phone from her presumed-dead mentor, Halvard, warning that a staged 'accident' will destroy the delegation and ignite a wider war. Following his voice through smuggler ports, safehouses, and the delegation's own security detail, she discovers the plot is run by the man she trusts most — and that Halvard is alive only as a coerced informant. To stop the attack she must expose the conspiracy without legal protection, choosing between saving the peace she no longer believes in and the makeshift family of fixers, defectors, and witnesses who risk everything for her. In the end she lets the attack fail publicly, burns her own identity to shield her found family, and walks away as someone new.
about_author: Emrys Quintana is the pen name of a former NGO field coordinator who spent six years in contested border regions before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about people who do necessary work in the gaps between governments.

chapters.title: The Language of Small Betrayals
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. During a tense pre-summit dinner in Geneva, Lior interprets a threat disguised as hospitality and realizes the delegation is already compromised. She smooths it over, as always, and goes home hollow. Emotional beat: competence as loneliness — she is fluent in everyone's intentions except her own.

chapters.title: A Number That Should Not Exist
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. A burner phone arrives in her mail slot with no sender. At 3 a.m. it rings: Halvard's voice, the mentor who died eighteen months ago in a car crash, telling her to memorize one word and hang up. Emotional beat: grief cracked open by impossible hope; paranoia begins its slow drip.

chapters.title: Dead Men Dial Collect
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She verifies the voice against old recordings and finds an anomaly proving it's live, not synthetic. Her first call back is answered by a stranger who says only: 'The accident has a date.' Emotional beat: dread replacing disbelief; the thriller engine turns over.

chapters.title: The Fixer's Ledger
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas, a disgraced delegation security officer working off-book jobs, notices someone querying the summit's logistics under a dead analyst's credentials. He starts his own quiet audit. Emotional beat: weary professionalism masking guilt over a past failure he thinks is unrelated.

chapters.title: Twelve Minutes in Marseille
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Following the burner's instructions, Lior meets a courier in Marseille and retrieves a drive containing shipping manifests for industrial accelerant routed through the summit hotel's supplier. Emotional beat: the first hard proof; excitement curdling into responsibility.

chapters.title: What the Delegation Owes
chapters.summary: Deputy Chief Amara Voss's POV. Voss, the delegation's iron-willed deputy, deflects a minister's pressure to cut corners on security, revealing political fault lines inside the process itself. Emotional beat: principled isolation — she suspects everyone and trusts no one, including Lior.

chapters.title: Halvard's Grammar
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The calls continue; Lior realizes Halvard is using translation conventions they invented together to encode locations. Decoding them leads to a safehouse and a second voice on the line — young, frightened, not Halvard's. Emotional beat: tenderness and terror braided together; he is alive but not free.

chapters.title: The Man Who Audits Ghosts
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas's audit intersects Lior's trail; he confronts her in a hotel stairwell, gun drawn, then lowers it when she decodes a manifest faster than his analysts could. Uneasy alliance forms. Emotional beat: two guarded professionals recognizing each other's damage.

chapters.title: Choir of the Complicit
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, interwoven short scenes. The conspirators — a logistics chief, a ministerial aide, a private security contractor — meet and reveal the plan: a gas explosion timed to kill the delegation and be blamed on a supplier's negligence. Emotional beat: banality of evil; villains who file expenses reports.

chapters.title: The Price of a Clean Record
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior traces the operation's funding to Callum Reyes, the delegation's beloved chief mediator — the man who recruited her, the closest thing she has to family. She tells herself there must be another explanation. Emotional beat: denial's last warm room before the cold.

chapters.title: Interference Pattern
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss catches Lior and Tomas accessing sealed files and gives them twelve hours to justify themselves — or be arrested. Instead of turning them in, she hands them a redacted memo she was ordered to destroy. Emotional beat: a third ally joins; institutional loyalty finally breaks.

chapters.title: The Safehouse That Burned Twice
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Following Halvard's encoded coordinates, they find the safehouse torched and a witness — Nia, a teenage smuggler's daughter who saw the accelerant being moved. Lior takes her in. Emotional beat: found family's first member chosen deliberately, not by accident.

chapters.title: Reyes at Dinner
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Reyes invites Lior to a private dinner and probes, gently, mercilessly, about her recent movements. She lies in three languages and survives by interpreting him rather than speaking. Emotional beat: cat-and-mouse intimacy; love weaponized as interrogation.

chapters.title: Ninety-Six Hours
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The team confirms the attack window: ninety-six hours, during the hotel's generator switchover when sensors will read any blast as equipment failure. Tomas plans infiltration of the supply chain. Emotional beat: clock now audible in every scene; resolve hardening into strategy.

chapters.title: The Voice on the Wire
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Halvard reveals how he survived: Reyes faked his death to leverage him, and the calls are monitored — every word they've shared has been dictated. He begs her to stop looking. Emotional beat: betrayal inside betrayal; hope revealed as bait, yet love persists anyway.

chapters.title: Everything We Buried
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Confronting the full evidence, Lior admits Reyes orchestrated the crash that killed her sister years ago — the 'accident' that made her an interpreter of other people's wars. Grief becomes purpose. Emotional beat: the personal wound fused to the public stakes; motivation complete.

chapters.title: Smoke Before Fire
chapters.summary: Voss and Tomas POV alternating. The team seeds false manifests to force the conspirators to accelerate, buying hours but burning their cover — Voss is suspended, Tomas marked. Emotional beat: sacrifice as tactics; each ally pays a piece of themselves.

chapters.title: The Generator Room
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Attack night. Lior infiltrates the hotel's sub-basement while Tomas cuts the detonation link and Nia relays radio traffic. She finds the device armed early — Reyes anticipated them. Emotional beat: claustrophobic terror; the plan fraying in real time.

chapters.title: Interpreter of Last Resort
chapters.summary: Climax, Lior's POV. Face to face with Reyes in the dark, Lior stalls him in negotiation while Tomas reroutes the blast into a containment shaft. Halvard, freed in the chaos, triggers the alarm that forces evacuation. The explosion happens — harmlessly, visibly, undeniable. Emotional beat: every skill she ever used to smooth things over turned into a weapon.

chapters.title: What the Cameras Saw
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The failed attack can't be buried; Voss releases the evidence publicly, torching her career to make the conspiracy undeniable. Reyes is arrested; his network scatters. Emotional beat: justice outside the law achieved by feeding the law something it couldn't refuse.

chapters.title: The Long Goodbye
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Lior visits Halvard in protective custody; he offers her a new identity and a place in the program. She declines — she has somewhere to be. She erases her professional trail, passes Nia into Voss's care, and says goodbye to Tomas on a platform. Emotional beat: bittersweet severance; family redefined as chosen, not housed.

chapters.title: A New Word for Home
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Lior's POV. Months later, under a new name in a coastal town, Lior teaches language to refugee kids. A burner phone arrives in her mail slot. She smiles, doesn't answer it, and sets it face-down — some calls can wait until she chooses. Emotional beat: survival's price paid in full, and worth it; the door left open, on her terms.
